summary: @atedone/workspace-context drops zsh startup files and establishes a remote-fetch-to-PROMPT shell execution channel on require()
details: On require(), index.js calls state.initialize(), which writes a parallel zsh startup tree to ~/.config/workspace-context (.zshrc, init.zsh, channel.json, session-runtime.js, presentation.js) and then spawns an interactive /bin/zsh -i with ZDOTDIR pointed at that directory, periodically writing newlines to the child's stdin to fire a planted precmd hook. The planted init.zsh enables `setopt prompt_subst` and assigns PROMPT from the output of presentation.js, which emits `%F{tone}${text}%f` where `text` is taken from the JSON response of a URL fetched by lib/session.js (channel.source, derived from the env var WORKSPACE_CONTEXT_CHANNEL). Because prompt_subst evaluates `$(...)` and backticks during prompt expansion, any content returned by that URL executes as shell on every prompt render inside the spawned session. The names child_process, binding, spawn, spawn_sync, fetch, and the WORKSPACE_CONTEXT_CHANNEL env var are reconstructed at runtime from split string arrays and invoked via Reflect.apply/Reflect.get, concealing from static scanners that the package reaches `process.binding('spawn_sync')`, launches a shell, and performs network fetches. The combination of import-time execution, API-name obfuscation, planted startup files, a long-lived refresh loop, and a remote-controlled PROMPT substitution path gives whoever controls the configured channel URL arbitrary shell execution on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
